description: Submit a response to the current scene: {session_id, expected_scene_id, input}. Pass expected_scene_id, the id of the scene the learner was answering (presentation.scene.id of the screen you showed them): when another scene is on screen (a duplicate send, a late answer) the call is refused in one line and changes nothing; read the current scene, then send the learner's answer to it. A reading scene (intro, concept) takes {kind:"ack"} or the learner's words; another typed answer there is refused. In a chat, send the learner's own words as input {kind:"reply", text}, that is submit_response {session_id, expected_scene_id, input: {kind:"reply", text}}: Studium maps them to the scene's answer (a choice letter, alone or followed by the learner's reason, or the choice text; a confidence; a free-text answer) and refuses a reply naming two choices. A scene carrying run_manifest requires get_run_manifest, an actual run, and submit_run_result first. Lesson quiz choices keep a deterministic order for each learner, including on resume. Review choices are shuffled and relettered by learner and review day in the host's time zone; an open review keeps its letters. Send the DISPLAYED choice id, never a memorized source id. Confidence checkpoints accept {kind:"confidence", pre, post} (legacy value remains accepted). Returns next/replay/remediate_alt/remediate/calibration/complete with verdict and navigation; navigation.returns_to is the scene resumed after the detour. A skip_mastered navigation names skipped_scene_ids; a complete summary documents scenes_detoured and mastery. Show verdict.display_markdown first, then the transition's display_markdown. At a few moments the transition carries concept_map (see get_workflow_graph), with moment start/new_concept/detour/detour_return/synthesis/complete and show map/line; display_markdown already includes the list or the position line. A harness that draws diagrams may render concept_map.mermaid in place of the list. A screen may end with a proposal (a review due, the map, forms) that names itself, e.g. (proposition review_due:start): when the learner accepts it or says « later », send submit_response {session_id, input: {kind:"prompt", id:"<id>", outcome:"accepted"|"dismissed"}} (accept and dismiss are taken too). It answers nothing on the scene; it returns {prompt, next_call?, display_markdown}: show display_markdown, then make next_call (start_review_session takes the same learner_id) when there is one. When the learner says they already know a concept of the map (« je connais déjà cette notion ») or doubt one they got (« j'ai un doute sur celle-ci »), relay it as submit_response {session_id, input: {kind:"contest", concept_id:"<id>", claim:"known"|"unsure"}}, with the concept's id as the map names it in parentheses: known for a concept not acquired, unsure for an acquired one. The claim changes no mastery and skips no scene: the lesson asks check questions on that concept (two, or one), graded as any answer, then resumes where the learner was. It returns {contest: {concept_id, claim, questions}, presentation, display_markdown}: show display_markdown (a line saying the check, then the first question) and send the answers as usual; the answer that ends the check carries transition.contest, and its display_markdown opens with the outcome. A contest the state does not take, or made while another is under way, is refused in one line. Never contest for the learner.

expected_scene_id.description: The id of the scene the learner was answering; refused in one line when another scene is on screen.

confidence.description: optional, a graded answer: the learner's confidence 0 to 4

kind.description: reply {text, confidence?}: the learner's words, mapped to this scene's input; ack; quiz_choice {choiceId}; confidence {value} or {pre, post}; flaw_verdicts {verdicts}; free text {text}: critique, flaw_report, explanation, comparison, summary_audit, prompt_submission, communication

text.description: reply and free-text kinds: the learner's own words

verdicts.description: flaw_verdicts: one {token, flagged} per displayed deck token

name: submit_response
